question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.
I am sure / that he will praying / for a good crop / this year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. that he will praying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "that he will praying" contains a grammatical error because the modal auxiliary "will" must be followed by the base form (V1) of the verb, not the present participle (V-ing) form.

• Rule — Modal + Verb: Modals such as will, shall, can, could, may, might, must, should are always followed by the first form of the verb (V1) without "to". If continuous action is intended, the correct structure is will + be + V-ing.
◦ Correct: that he will pray for a good crop this year. (simple future)
◦ Also correct: that he will be praying for a good crop this year. (future continuous)

• The given phrase "will praying" wrongly combines the modal directly with the -ing form, omitting the auxiliary "be", which is grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "I am sure" is grammatically correct — Subject + is/am/are is a standard present tense structure and introduces the subordinate clause correctly.

• Option 3: "this year." is grammatically correct — it is a simple time adverbial with no error.

• Option 4: "for a good crop" is grammatically correct — a correctly formed prepositional phrase.

NOTE

• Common modal errors tested by SSC: "will can", "must to", "should to" (double modals/infinitive after modal) are always incorrect.

• Remember: modal + V1 always; never modal + V-ing or modal + V3 directly.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
My students are / waiting for / their flights / at the gate no. 6.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. at the gate no. 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "at the gate no. 6." contains a grammatical error because the definite article "the" is not used before an identifying number introduced by "no." (number), such as gate number, room number, page number, platform number, etc.

• Rule — Articles with "No. + Number": When a common noun is followed by "no." + a specific number, it functions like a proper name/unique identifier, so the article "the" is dropped.
◦ Correct: at gate no. 6 / in room no. 5 / on page no. 10 / from platform no. 3.

• The correct sentence should read: "My students are waiting for their flights at gate no. 6."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "waiting for" is grammatically correct — the present continuous verb correctly agrees with the plural subject "students".

• Option 3: "their flights" is grammatically correct — the possessive pronoun "their" correctly agrees with the plural subject "students".

• Option 4: "My students are" is grammatically correct — subject-verb agreement is correct (plural subject with "are").

NOTE

• Similar "no. + number" constructions frequently tested: seat no. 12, bus no. 45, flight no. 202, ward no. 3 — none of these take "the" before them.

• However, when referring to the general noun without a number (e.g., "the gate", "the room"), the article "the" IS required.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
I am very much / obliged of my friend / for the help / he rendered to me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. obliged of my friend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "obliged of my friend" contains a grammatical error because the adjective "obliged" (meaning grateful/indebted) takes the preposition "to", not "of", when referring to the person one is grateful to.

• Rule — Preposition with "obliged": Obliged to (a person) = grateful/indebted to someone; obliged to (do something) = compelled/required to do something. It is never followed by "of".
◦ Correct: I am very much obliged to my friend for the help he rendered to me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "I am very much" is grammatically correct — a standard intensifier phrase before an adjective.

• Option 2: "he rendered to me" is grammatically correct — "render help to someone" is a correct collocation.

• Option 3: "for the help" is grammatically correct — correct preposition "for" is used with "help" here, indicating reason/purpose.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused prepositions with adjectives tested by SSC: grateful to (a person) / grateful for (a thing), thankful to / thankful for, indebted to.

• Remember: "obliged" never takes "of" — a very common SSC error-spotting trap.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
She will being studying for her exams tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will being.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "will being" contains a grammatical error. The Future Continuous Tense requires the structure will + be + V-ing, not will + being.

• Rule — Future Continuous Tense: Subject + will/shall + be + V-ing + Object. The auxiliary after "will" must be the base form "be", never its -ing form "being".
◦ Correct: She will be studying for her exams tomorrow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "studying" is grammatically correct — it is the correct -ing form required after "will be" in the future continuous structure.

• Option 2: "tomorrow" is grammatically correct — a correct time adverb consistent with the future tense.

• Option 4: "exams" is grammatically correct — correctly used plural noun with the possessive "her".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "being" (the -ing form of "be", used as a gerund/participle, e.g. "Being late, he apologised") with the plain auxiliary "be" required after modals like will/shall/can/should.

• Other future continuous examples: I will be traveling tomorrow; They will be waiting at the station.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Oil is almost certainly one of the ocean’s greatest resources. 33% of the world’s oil comes from seaward fields in seas. Oils are liquids that easily burn and do not (1)______ in water. Most of the time, they are made of chains of carbon and hydrogen atoms. There are three (2)______ types of oils: mineral, essential and fixed oils. From plants, essential oils are thin, scented oils. Because they frequently have an odour, essential oils are (3)______ in perfumery and food flavouring. Aromatic extraction processes like cold pressing, distillation and extraction are typically used to prepare essential oils. Fatty acids are used by animals and plants to make fixed oils. They are especially non-volatile oils that are found in the seeds of cotton, corn, flax, sunflowers, peanuts, coconuts and olives, as well as in fatty animal tissues. Mineral oils are (4)________ from petroleum which has been underground for millions of years from sea organism skeletons. Mineral oils are one of the petroleum by-products with the lowest prices. Mineral oils are colourless and transparent. They are made up of a (5)_____ of hydrocarbons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dissolve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "dissolve" means to become mixed with a liquid so as to form a solution, i.e., to blend completely into a liquid.

• In the given context, oils are described as substances that do not mix with / blend into water — since oil and water do not form a homogeneous solution, the correct word is "dissolve".
◦ Example: Sugar dissolves in water, but oil does not dissolve in water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "diffuse" means to spread out or disperse gradually — it does not fit the specific idea of forming a solution with water.

• Option 3: "melt" means to change from a solid to a liquid state due to heat — oil is already a liquid here, so this does not fit the context.

• Option 4: "evaporate" means to change from liquid to vapour/gas — this is unrelated to mixing with water.

NOTE

• Commonly confused words: dissolve (form a solution), melt (solid to liquid), evaporate (liquid to gas), diffuse (spread out) — each describes a distinct physical process and SSC frequently tests the difference in cloze passages.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. primary.

• The word "primary" means main, principal, or most important — used here to describe the three main/basic categories or types of oils.

• In the given context, the passage is classifying oils into their main/basic types (mineral, essential and fixed), so "primary types" is the most natural and appropriate collocation.
◦ Example: There are three primary colours — red, blue and yellow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "initial" means happening at the beginning — it does not fit the idea of classifying types.

• Option 2: "original" means the first or earliest version of something — it does not fit a classification context.

• Option 3: "early" relates to time (occurring before the expected time) — it is unrelated to classifying types of oils.

NOTE

• "Primary" is commonly used before classification nouns: primary colours, primary sources, primary categories, primary types — a frequently tested collocation in SSC cloze passages.

Most of the time, they are made of chains of carbon and hydrogen atoms. There are three (2)______ types of oils: mineral, essential and fixed oils. From plants, essential oils are thin, scented oils. Aromatic extraction processes like cold pressing, distillation and extraction are typically used to prepare essential oils. Fatty acids are used by animals and plants to make fixed oils. They are especially non-volatile oils that are found in the seeds of cotton, corn, flax, sunflowers, peanuts, coconuts and olives, as well as in fatty animal tissues. Mineral oils are (4)________ from petroleum which has been underground for millions of years from sea organism skeletons. Mineral oils are one of the petroleum by-products with the lowest prices. Mineral oils are colourless and transparent. They are made up of a (5)_____ of hydrocarbons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. utilised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "utilised" means made practical and effective use of something — it correctly conveys the idea that essential oils are put to use in perfumery and food flavouring because of their odour.

• In the given context, the passage explains that because essential oils have a strong smell, they are used/put to practical use in perfumery and flavouring industries — "utilised" best fits this sense of practical usage.
◦ Example: These essential oils are utilised in the manufacture of perfumes and flavoured foods.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "applied" means put into operation or brought into contact with something (e.g., applying a cream) — it does not naturally collocate with being "used" in an industry in this way.

• Option 3: "operated" means to control or run a machine or system — it does not fit the context of using oils for their fragrance.

• Option 4: "employed" means to use something/someone for a particular purpose, usually in relation to labour or a method — while close in meaning, it is a weaker collocation than "utilised" here for a raw material being put to practical use.

NOTE

• "Utilise/utilised" is commonly the preferred word in SSC cloze passages when describing a raw material or resource being put to practical use, as opposed to "employed" which more often refers to people or methods.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Oil is almost certainly one of the ocean’s greatest resources. 33% of the world’s oil comes from seaward fields in seas. Oils are liquids that easily burn and do not (1)______ in water. Most of the time, they are made of chains of carbon and hydrogen atoms. There are three (2)______ types of oils: mineral, essential and fixed oils. From plants, essential oils are thin, scented oils. Because they frequently have an odour, essential oils are (3)______ in perfumery and food flavouring. Aromatic extraction processes like cold pressing, distillation and extraction are typically used to prepare essential oils. Fatty acids are used by animals and plants to make fixed oils. They are especially non-volatile oils that are found in the seeds of cotton, corn, flax, sunflowers, peanuts, coconuts and olives, as well as in fatty animal tissues. Mineral oils are (4)________ from petroleum which has been underground for millions of years from sea organism skeletons. Mineral oils are one of the petroleum by-products with the lowest prices. Mineral oils are colourless and transparent. They are made up of a (5)_____ of hydrocarbons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. produced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "produced" means brought into existence or made from raw material through a natural or industrial process — it correctly describes how mineral oils are derived/made from petroleum.

• In the given context, mineral oils come from petroleum that has been underground for millions of years, so "produced from petroleum" correctly expresses their natural origin.
◦ Example: Plastic is produced from petroleum-based chemicals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "invented" means to create something new that did not exist before (typically a device or idea) — mineral oils are naturally derived, not invented.

• Option 3: "renewed" means to make something valid or new again — this does not fit the idea of a substance being derived from a natural source.

• Option 4: "fabricated" means to construct or manufacture, often also implying something false/made-up — it does not fit the natural process of oil formation described here.

NOTE

• Distinguish: produced (naturally/industrially made from raw material), invented (create something new/original), fabricated (manufactured, or falsely made up), renewed (made new/extended again) — a common vocabulary distinction tested in SSC cloze passages.

Most of the time, they are made of chains of carbon and hydrogen atoms. There are three (2)______ types of oils: mineral, essential and fixed oils. From plants, essential oils are thin, scented oils. Aromatic extraction processes like cold pressing, distillation and extraction are typically used to prepare essential oils. Fatty acids are used by animals and plants to make fixed oils. They are especially non-volatile oils that are found in the seeds of cotton, corn, flax, sunflowers, peanuts, coconuts and olives, as well as in fatty animal tissues. Mineral oils are (4)________ from petroleum which has been underground for millions of years from sea organism skeletons. Mineral oils are one of the petroleum by-products with the lowest prices. Mineral oils are colourless and transparent. They are made up of a (5)_____ of hydrocarbons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. combination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "combination" means a joining or mixture of two or more different things — it correctly describes mineral oils as being made up of a mixture of different hydrocarbons.

• In the given context, the sentence describes what mineral oils are chemically composed of, so "a combination of hydrocarbons" correctly expresses this mixture.
◦ Example: Petrol is a combination of various hydrocarbons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "collaboration" means working jointly with others, typically people or organisations — it does not apply to chemical substances.

• Option 2: "cooperation" means working together helpfully, again typically applying to people — it is not used to describe the chemical composition of a substance.

• Option 4: "association" means a group of people/organisations joined for a common purpose, or a mental connection between ideas — it does not fit the chemical/compositional sense required here.

NOTE

• "Combination" is the correct word when describing a mixture of substances/elements, while "collaboration" and "cooperation" apply specifically to people or organisations working together — a common trap in SSC cloze passages.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Merit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fault.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Merit" means a good quality, virtue, or worth that deserves praise or reward. (गुण/योग्यता)
◦ Example: Hard work and honesty are among his greatest merits.

• The antonym of "Merit" is "Fault", which means a defect, flaw, or shortcoming. (दोष/खामी)
◦ Example: His biggest fault is that he loses his temper too quickly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Result" (परिणाम): means the outcome or consequence of an action — unrelated to "merit" as an antonym.

• Option 2: "Tumult" (हंगामा): means a loud, confused noise or disturbance — unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Occult" (गूढ़/रहस्यमय): means secret, mysterious, or related to the supernatural — unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other synonym-antonym pairs of "merit" often tested: synonyms — virtue, worth, excellence; antonyms — demerit, defect, flaw, vice.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence.
I am contant with my day’s work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. content.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "content" — here used as an adjective meaning satisfied or at ease with one's situation. (संतुष्ट)
◦ Example: After finishing the project on time, she felt content with her day's work.

• Spelling key: CON + TENT. Remember it is spelled the same as the noun "content" (meaning "what is contained"), though the meaning here is different (adjective = satisfied).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "contint" — incorrect; the second syllable "tint" is a misspelling of "tent".

• Option 2: "contante" — incorrect; an extra "a" and "e" have been wrongly inserted.

• Option 4: "cuntent" — incorrect; the first vowel "o" has been wrongly replaced with "u".

NOTE

• "Content" can be both a noun (/ˈkɒntent/, meaning "what is contained", e.g. "the content of the book") and an adjective (/kənˈtent/, meaning "satisfied"), spelled identically but pronounced differently.

• Related words: contentment (noun), contentedly (adverb).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The ________ in my shoelace created a lot of trouble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. knot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "knot" means a fastening made by tying a piece of string, rope, or lace, and fits the context of a shoelace causing trouble. (गांठ)
◦ Example: He struggled for five minutes to undo the knot in his shoelace.

• The correct sentence is: "The knot in my shoelace created a lot of trouble.", referring to a tangled/tightly-tied lace.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "not" is a negative particle (adverb of negation) and makes no sense as the subject of the sentence.

• Option 2: "naught" means nothing or zero — it does not fit the context of a shoelace.

• Option 3: "nought" also means zero/nothing (British spelling) — it does not fit the context either.

NOTE

• "Knot", "not", "naught" and "nought" are commonly confused homophones/near-homophones in SSC vocabulary questions — knot (a fastening), not (negation), naught/nought (zero, nothing).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
If you are thinking about investing in share markets, isn’t it make sense to find an expert?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. doesn't it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause of the sentence is "it make sense to find an expert", which is in the Simple Present Tense with the base verb "make" governed by the third-person singular subject "it".

• Rule — Question tag/emphatic structure with Simple Present: For a third-person singular subject in the simple present, the auxiliary used is does/doesn't, and since the main verb here is in its base form ("make", not "makes"), the correct auxiliary is the negative "doesn't", matching the structure "doesn't it make sense".

• Applying the rule: "isn't it make sense" is grammatically wrong because "isn't" (a form of "to be") cannot be paired with the base verb "make". The correct auxiliary is "doesn't it".
◦ Correct: If you are thinking about investing in share markets, doesn't it make sense to find an expert?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "did it" is incorrect because it uses the past tense auxiliary "did", which does not agree with the present tense verb "make" and overall present context of the sentence.

• Option 2: "is it" is incorrect because "is" (a "to be" verb) cannot combine directly with the base verb "make"; it would require "makes" instead.

• Option 4: "do it" is incorrect because the subject "it" is third-person singular, requiring "does", not "do".

NOTE

• This is not a simple question-tag but an embedded question structure using "doesn't it + V1" for rhetorical emphasis, common in SSC grammar questions.

• Remember: with "to be" verbs (is/am/are), never combine directly with a base-form action verb like "make" — use "does/do/did" as the supporting auxiliary instead.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Important
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Trivial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Important" means having great significance or value; of much consequence. (महत्वपूर्ण)
◦ Example: Education is an important factor in a country's development.

• The antonym of "Important" is "Trivial", which means of little value or importance; insignificant. (तुच्छ/मामूली)
◦ Example: He got upset over a trivial matter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Recurring" (बार-बार होने वाला): means happening repeatedly — unrelated in meaning to "important".

• Option 2: "Productive" (उत्पादक): means producing good results or yielding a lot — unrelated as an antonym here.

• Option 4: "Significant" (महत्वपूर्ण): is actually a synonym of "important" (both mean noteworthy/of consequence), not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "important": significant, crucial, vital, essential. Other antonyms: trivial, insignificant, negligible, unimportant.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Independence Day is considered as a red-letter day in the history of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Memorable day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Red-letter day" means a special, memorable, or particularly significant day, one worth remembering and celebrating. (यादगार/विशेष दिन)
◦ Example: Their wedding anniversary is always a red-letter day for the couple.

• The expression originates from the old practice of marking festivals, holidays, and other special days in red ink on calendars, distinguishing them from ordinary days marked in black.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Regular day" (सामान्य दिन): means an ordinary, usual day — the opposite of what the idiom conveys.

• Option 2: "Uneventful day" (नीरस दिन): means a day with nothing noteworthy happening — again opposite in sense.

• Option 4: "Unimportant day" (महत्वहीन दिन): means a day of no significance — this is contrary to the idiom's actual meaning.

NOTE

• Other calendar-related idioms tested by SSC: "Once in a blue moon" (very rarely), "In broad daylight" (openly, during the day), "D-day" (the decisive/crucial day).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, that have always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. which was always silently rolling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the relative clause is "a mighty river", which is a singular, non-human/inanimate noun, and the clause is a non-restrictive (non-defining) relative clause set off by a comma (giving extra information about the river).

• Rule — Relative Pronouns: For non-human/inanimate antecedents, "which" is used, not "that", especially in a non-defining clause introduced by a comma (a comma before "that" is not standard). The verb must agree with the singular subject "river", so the auxiliary should be "was", not "have"/"were".

• Applying the rule: the pronoun should be "which" (non-human, non-restrictive clause) and the auxiliary should be "was" (agreeing with the singular "river"), with the main verb in its correct continuous form "rolling".
◦ Correct: He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, which was always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "which were always silently rolling" is incorrect because "were" is plural, but the antecedent "river" is singular.

• Option 3: "that were always silently rolling" is incorrect on two counts: "that" is not used after a comma in a non-defining clause, and "were" wrongly treats "river" as plural.

• Option 4: "what has always silently rolling" is incorrect because "what" is never used as a relative pronoun referring back to a stated antecedent like "river", and "has...rolling" is not a valid verb form (missing "been").

NOTE

• Comma + "that" is never grammatically acceptable in standard English — always use "which" or "who" after a comma to introduce a non-defining relative clause.

• Remember: use "who/whom" for people, "which" for things/animals, and "that" for either but only in defining (non-comma) clauses.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
Namita still cannot _________ the pain of her cat’s untimely demise.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. bear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "bear" (verb) means to endure or tolerate something difficult or painful, which fits the context of Namita being unable to endure the pain of her cat's death.
◦ Example: I cannot bear to see him in so much pain.

• Homophone note: "bear" (to endure/a large animal) is being tested against similarly-sounding words — "bier" (a stand on which a coffin is placed) and "beer" (an alcoholic drink) sound similar but are spelled and mean differently, while "bare" (meaning uncovered/empty) is a near-homophone with a different spelling and meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "bier" means a movable frame on which a coffin or corpse is placed — it does not fit the verb slot required by the sentence.

• Option 3: "beer" refers to an alcoholic beverage — completely unrelated to the context.

• Option 4: "bare" means uncovered, empty, or plain (adjective/verb "to bare") — it does not convey the sense of "enduring pain" needed here.

NOTE

• Homophones commonly tested by SSC: bear/bare, beer/bier, meet/meat, wait/weight, sale/sail. Always judge by the meaning required in context, not just the sound.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
A sailor was __________through the high tides.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sailing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "sailing" (from the verb "to sail", meaning to travel on water in a boat/ship) correctly fits the context of a sailor navigating through high tides.
◦ Example: The sailor was sailing skilfully through the rough sea.

• The sentence logically connects the subject "sailor" with the action of "sailing", which is his defining activity, especially through difficult conditions like high tides.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "ceiling" refers to the upper interior surface of a room, or (as a noun) an upper limit — it is unrelated to a sailor's action and only superficially similar in sound/spelling to "sailing".

• Option 3: "swelling" means increasing in size/becoming swollen — while tides can "swell", the subject of the action here is the sailor, not the tide, so this does not fit grammatically.

• Option 4: "selling" means exchanging goods for money — entirely unrelated to the context of a sailor and tides.

NOTE

• This question tests near-homophones/similarly spelled words: sailing, ceiling, swelling, selling — always identify the word whose meaning logically fits the subject and context of the sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Vishnu and Vignesh are always like two peas in a pod.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Very similar to each other.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Like two peas in a pod" means two people (or things) that are extremely similar to each other, in appearance, character, or habits. (एक जैसे/हूबहू समान)
◦ Example: The twin sisters are like two peas in a pod — no one can tell them apart.

• The expression comes from the observation that peas growing together inside the same pod look nearly identical to one another.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Smart and intelligent" (होशियार और बुद्धिमान): describes mental ability, which is not what the idiom conveys.

• Option 3: "Happy and compassionate" (खुश और दयालु): describes emotional/character traits unrelated to the idea of similarity.

• Option 4: "Good in every way" (हर तरह से अच्छा): is a vague statement about quality, not about resemblance between two people.

NOTE

• Other similarity-based idioms tested by SSC: "Birds of a feather (flock together)" (people with similar traits associate with each other), "Cut from the same cloth" (having the same characteristics), "The spitting image of" (looking exactly like someone).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The crowd gave them a _________ of applause.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. round.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "a round of applause" is a fixed collocation meaning a burst of clapping by a group of people to show appreciation. (तालियों की गड़गड़ाहट)
◦ Example: The audience gave the performer a round of applause at the end of the show.

• "Round" here is used in its collocational sense of "a series or burst of something happening together", as in "a round of applause", "a round of drinks", or "a round of talks".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "yell" means a loud shout or cry — it does not collocate with "applause" and does not fit the fixed phrase.

• Option 2: "load" means a quantity carried or a burden — it is unrelated to the idiomatic phrase describing clapping.

• Option 3: "laugh" relates to the act of laughing, not clapping — irrelevant to the idea of "applause".

NOTE

• Other fixed collocations with "round": a round of talks, a round of drinks, a round of golf, a round of negotiations — a frequently tested vocabulary pattern in SSC exams.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
Applications are to be sent to the school’s e-mail ID before 30th June.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "are to be sent" is already grammatically correct. It uses the structure "is/are + to be + V3", which correctly expresses a passive obligation or planned/scheduled action — something that is required or expected to be done.

• Rule — Passive obligation structure: Subject + is/are + to be + V3 (past participle) is used to state a formal instruction, requirement, or planned future action in the passive voice.
◦ Example: The report is to be submitted by Friday. / The forms are to be filled before the deadline.

• Since "Applications are to be sent to the school's e-mail ID" correctly conveys the required action in the passive voice, no change/substitution is needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "will be send to" is incorrect because after the passive auxiliary "will be", the verb must be in its past participle (V3) form "sent", not the base form "send".

• Option 2: "is sending" is incorrect because it wrongly uses the singular auxiliary "is" for the plural subject "Applications", and the active continuous form does not convey the same sense of formal requirement.

• Option 4: "would be send to" is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1 — the past participle "sent" is required after "be", not "send"; also "would" incorrectly shifts the sentence's tone from a present instruction to a conditional one.

NOTE

• Always check whether the underlined portion is already correct before assuming an error exists — SSC frequently includes "No substitution/improvement required" as the correct option to test this.

• Remember: after any form of "be" (is/are/was/were/be/been/being), the main verb must be in its past participle (V3) form to form the passive voice.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Advertisment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Advertisement" — a notice or announcement promoting a product, service, or event. (विज्ञापन)
◦ Example: The company released a new advertisement for its latest smartphone.

• Spelling key: ADVERTISE + MENT. The base verb "advertise" keeps its final "e" before adding the suffix "-ment", giving advertise + ment = advertisement. The option "Advertisment" wrongly drops this "e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Adulterous" is spelt correctly — meaning relating to adultery/impurity.

• Option 2: "Amendment" is spelt correctly — meaning a minor change or addition, especially to a law or document.

• Option 4: "Astounding" is spelt correctly — meaning extremely surprising or impressive.

NOTE

• Common misspellings to watch for around "-ment" suffix words: judgement/judgment (both accepted), argument (drops the "e" from "argue"), advertisement (keeps the "e") — spelling rules with silent "e" before suffixes are frequently tested by SSC.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The painting look good in this room.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. looks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The painting", which is a singular, third-person noun. In the Simple Present Tense, a singular third-person subject requires the verb to take an -s/-es ending.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement (Simple Present): Singular subject (he/she/it/singular noun) + V1 + s/es. The base verb "look" must become "looks" to agree with the singular subject "the painting".
◦ Correct: The painting looks good in this room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "have looking" is incorrect — this is not a valid verb form; "have" would require a past participle ("have looked"), not the -ing form.

• Option 2: "looking" is incorrect on its own, as a bare present participle cannot function as the main verb of the sentence without an auxiliary like "is".

• Option 3: "had look" is incorrect — "had" (past perfect auxiliary) must be followed by a past participle ("had looked"), not the base form "look", and it also shifts the tense incorrectly.

NOTE

• Common subject-verb agreement traps in SSC: singular collective/abstract nouns like "the painting", "the news", "the team" (when treated as a single unit) all take a singular verb.

• Remember: Simple Present + singular subject → verb + s/es; Simple Present + plural subject → verb without s/es.

question:
Replace the underlined word in the given sentence with an appropriate synonym from the options listed below.
They gave us the impression that Clara was a cold and calculating woman, who was only after power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. manipulative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "calculating" (as used here to describe a person) means shrewdly and selfishly scheming or planning things to gain an advantage over others, often without regard for other people's feelings. (चालाक/स्वार्थी योजनाकार)
◦ Example: He is a cold and calculating businessman who thinks only of profit.

• "Manipulative" means skilfully and often unfairly controlling or influencing people or situations for one's own benefit, which closely matches the sense of a person who is "calculating" in their dealings with others.
◦ Example: She used manipulative tactics to get what she wanted from her colleagues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "callous" means showing a cruel disregard for others' feelings — it conveys insensitivity, not the scheming/self-serving planning implied by "calculating".

• Option 2: "unscrupulous" means having or showing no moral principles — it is close in tone but refers more broadly to lacking scruples/ethics generally, rather than specifically the scheming, self-interested planning in "calculating".

• Option 3: "unsympathetic" means not feeling or showing sympathy or pity for others — it only captures the "coldness" aspect and misses the "scheming for advantage" sense that "calculating" specifically conveys.

NOTE

• Words describing a scheming/self-interested personality often tested together: manipulative, cunning, scheming, shrewd, calculating — while words like callous, unsympathetic, unscrupulous are related but emphasise different shades of negative character (lack of feeling, lack of ethics).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Gentlemen always go for a lawful approach, but rouges choose ______ ways to solve problems.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. illicit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lawful" means permitted by or in accordance with the law; legal. (कानूनी/वैध)
◦ Example: Every citizen has the lawful right to vote.

• The antonym of "lawful" is "illicit", which means forbidden by law, rules, or custom; illegal. (अवैध/गैरकानूनी)
◦ Example: The police raided the market to stop the illicit sale of drugs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "legal" (कानूनी): is a synonym of "lawful" (both mean permitted by law), not its antonym.

• Option 2: "legitimate" (वैध): is also a synonym of "lawful", meaning conforming to the law or accepted rules.

• Option 3: "sophisticated" (परिष्कृत): means having refined knowledge, culture, or complexity — unrelated in meaning to "lawful"/"unlawful".

NOTE

• Other synonym-antonym sets around "lawful" often tested: synonyms — legal, legitimate, licit, permissible; antonyms — illegal, illicit, unlawful, illegitimate.
